subject: اللغة الإنجليزية
lesson: Lesson 2: WOW! Team Talk – Are extreme sports dangerous?
outcomes: Understand a dialogue where two friends disagree about extreme sports.
Use I suppose so., I told you so! and Not really. correctly.
Give your opinion about extreme sports with a reason.

tf.s: Ali and Eric disagree about whether extreme sports are too dangerous for children.
tf.why: Yes, that is what the boys talk about.

tf.s: Eric hurt himself when he was go-karting.
tf.why: Eric fell when he was rock climbing.

tf.s: Eric’s cousin started sandboarding when he was four.
Eric’s cousin never uses a helmet.
tf.why: He always uses a helmet and wears special clothes.

tf.s: Eric’s sister cut herself when she was running.
tf.why: Right! Eric uses this to show all sports can be dangerous.

tf.s: Ali thinks children shouldn’t do extreme sports because they often hurt themselves.
At the end, the boys are going to the beach.
We say “I told you so!” when we were right before.
tf.why: Great! It shows you said it earlier.
Not really. is a soft way to say no.

tf.s: Eric thinks only extreme sports can be dangerous.
tf.why: Eric says all sports can be dangerous.

o: He fell when he was rock climbing.

boxes.q: Who said: “That’s too young. What if he hurts himself?”
boxes.why: Ali worries that children get hurt.

boxes.q: Where are the boys going at the end?
boxes.why: They go to their PE lesson.

boxes.q: Which expression means you were right before?
boxes.why: I told you so! shows you said it first.

boxes.q: “Was the test difficult yesterday?” (It was easy.)
boxes.why: Not really. means no, not much.

boxes.q: “If you like cycling, you’ll like mountain biking.”
boxes.why: I suppose so. means you agree a little.

boxes.q: He always ___ a helmet and wears special clothes.
boxes.why: Eric’s cousin always uses a helmet.

boxes.q: Who is with Eric’s cousin when he goes sandboarding?
boxes.why: His parents are there to keep him safe.

boxes.q: “That bus to the beach was very slow!”
boxes.why: You said before that the bus was slow.

boxes.q: What does the safety gear protect you from?
boxes.why: Helmets and special clothes help stop injuries.

hunt.q: A soft way to say no:
The boys go to ___ at the end.
Who thinks extreme sports are risky?

mcq.q: What do Ali and Eric disagree about?
o: Whether extreme sports are too dangerous for children
mcq.why: That is the main topic of the dialogue.

mcq.q: How does Eric show that all sports can be dangerous?
o: His sister cut herself when she was running.
His cousin fell off a cliff.

mcq.q: How does Eric’s cousin stay safe?
o: He uses a helmet, wears special clothes and his parents are there.
mcq.why: Safety gear and his parents keep him safe.

mcq.q: Which expression shows you agree but not strongly?
mcq.why: I suppose so. is a weak agreement.

mcq.q: A: “Do you like snakes?” B: “___ They scare me.”
mcq.why: Not really. is a polite no.

mcq.q: A: “I said it would rain, and now it’s raining!” What could A say?
A: “Maybe we should take a helmet, just in case.” B (agreeing a little): “___”
mcq.why: I suppose so. is a soft yes.

mcq.q: Why does Ali think children shouldn’t do extreme sports?
Which reason best supports Eric’s opinion?
o: Children can be safe with a helmet, special clothes and parents there.
mcq.why: Eric shows how his cousin stays safe.

mcq.q: Which is the best way to give your opinion in this debate?
o: I agree with Eric because all sports can be dangerous.
mcq.why: A good opinion has a reason.
